stem: Which statement about head banging as a rhythmic movement in children is correct?

options.text: It typically begins at the end of the first year and stops before age 4
It is significantly more common in females than in males
It is usually associated with abnormal daytime behaviour or development
It rarely occurs in children who have previously shown body rocking
It usually begins in late adolescence

explanation: Head banging typically begins near the end of the first year of life and usually resolves before age 4.
rationale: It is a benign rhythmic movement of early childhood with a characteristic age range and usually normal daytime functioning.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because head banging typically starts towards the end of the first year and usually resolves before age 4.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because head banging is more common in males than in females.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because it is usually seen in otherwise healthy children and is not typically linked to abnormal daytime behaviour or development.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because head banging may occur alongside other rhythmic behaviours such as body rocking.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because head banging is a phenomenon of early childhood, not late adolescence.

source.hint: Consider the typical age range and developmental context for this behavior.
